### Definition of sine

For an angle with measure $\theta$ in a right triangle:

$\sin(\theta)=\dfrac{\blueE{\text{opposite leg length}}}{\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$

### Identifying the hypotenuse and the side opposite to $\angle B$

The side $\blueE{\text{opposite}}$ to $\angle B$ is $\overline{AC}$ and its length is $\blueE{12}$ units.

The $\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse}}$ is $\overline{AB}$ and its length is $\purpleD{13}$ units.

choices.clue:
This is the side *adjacent* to $\angle B$ divided by the hypotenuse.

But $\sin(\beta)$ is the side *opposite* to $\angle B$ divided by the hypotenuse.

This is the side opposite to $\angle B$ divided by the side *adjacent* to $\angle B$.

But $\sin(\beta)$ is the side opposite to $\angle B$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.

This is the side *adjacent* to $\angle B$ divided by the side *opposite* to $\angle B$.

But $\sin(\beta)$ is the side *opposite* to $\angle B$ divided by the *hypotenuse*.
